citation.authors: Özcan FÖ, Okudu C, Odabaş Hİ, Turan İT
citation.title: Acute effects of arabica and chicory coffee on exercise performance and post‐exercise biomarkers in young male adults: A controlled crossover study

population.description: Twenty-two moderately active young men aged 18-25 years (enrolment range, not observed min/max) who completed all sessions; screened with the PAR-Q+ for exercise contraindications (cardiovascular disease, chest pain, syncope, musculoskeletal condition, type 2 diabetes with hypoglycaemia history, others excluded); called healthy in the paper's abstract and conclusions. Age and BMI are mean ± SD at the reference assessment (Results 3.1).

protocols.name: control_fasted
protocols.description: No-coffee reference session (always the first session): participants attended each test after at least 8 h of fasting (a lower bound; 10 h is assumed), nothing drunk, with pre-exercise measurements taken before the 20-m shuttle-run test, which began at approximately 10:00. Only the pre-exercise values are entered; the paper does not say when in the morning, how long before the run, or after what rest they were taken, so a 31-minute fasted arm starting 09:30 and read at minute 30 (about 10:00) stands for them. No exercise input is written.

findings.description: Capillary blood glucose (meter not named; capillary whole-blood reading, not plasma) before exercise, no-coffee reference session, mean and SD

location.where: Table 3, row 'Blood glucose (mg/dL)', condition C, column 'Pre-exercise (mean ± SD)' (Table 1 prints 99.6 ± 8.8)

findings.description: Heart rate before exercise, no-coffee reference session, mean and SD

location.where: Table 1, row 'Heart rate (beats/min)', condition C, column 'Pre-exercise'

findings.description: Systolic blood pressure before exercise, no-coffee reference session, mean and SD

location.where: Table 3, row 'Systolic BP (mmHg)', condition C, column 'Pre-exercise (mean ± SD)' (Table 1 prints 117.9 ± 11.7)

findings.description: Diastolic blood pressure before exercise, no-coffee reference session, mean and SD

location.where: Table 3, row 'Diastolic BP (mmHg)', condition C, column 'Pre-exercise (mean ± SD)' (Table 1 prints 64.9 ± 10.9)

findings.description: Peripheral oxygen saturation before exercise, no-coffee reference session, mean and SD

location.where: Table 3, row 'SpO2 (%)', condition C, column 'Pre-exercise (mean ± SD)' (Table 1 prints 97.5 ± 1.0)

left_out.what: Heart rate, systolic and diastolic pressure, lactate, SpO2 and glucose immediately after the 20-m shuttle-run test to exhaustion and at 5 min of recovery (Tables 1 and 3, all three conditions): progressive field test with no printed oxygen uptake for the bout, no printed duration and a variable running speed

Blood lactate before exercise, control session (Lactate Scout 4; Tables 1 and 3, 3.20 +/- 2.54 mmol/L, n = 22): the paper does not say it was drawn at rest or after what rest, and a mean this high with an SD this wide (Arabica session 4.05 +/- 5.21) is not a resting value, so it cannot be placed at a state of the model

All values of the Arabica and chicory coffee sessions (Tables 1, 3, 4): 180 mL of coffee or chicory-root drink 45 min before the run; the beverages are not a meal or any input the model has, and their caffeine was not measured (estimated 80-100 mg for Arabica)
Post-exercise LPL (ng/mL), TNF-alpha, IL-6 (pg/mL) and adiponectin (ug/mL) by condition (Table 4): group values only, no SD or SEM printed, and measured only after the run
Borg perceived exertion score immediately after the run (Table 2)
Shuttle-run laps and VO2max estimated from the final level and laps by a published formula (Table 2): performance outcomes of the bout, not a measured oxygen uptake of the bout
